Aurora — Turin, Italy

🟠 Qualitative/limited official context

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

This is the official quartiere that contains Porta Palazzo — the example that inspired this whole project. The market itself is a genuine, safe daytime attraction, but the wider Aurora area has well-documented, recurring problems with drug dealing and decay that show up even in daylight and worsen at night. Despite this, some listings here get very high online reviews from tourists who never notice the difference.

Frequently asked questions

Is Aurora safe?

Wandroz currently rates Aurora in Turin, Italy as an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Turin, Italy during the day and an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Turin, Italy at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset or press research — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Aurora safe at night?

At night, Aurora is rated as an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Turin, Italy. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Aurora a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Aurora's day rating (an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Turin, Italy) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
